subject: Aurora Health: Data export justification and DPF supplemental evidence request
body:
Message 1/4
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@aurorahealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2029 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Data export justification and DPF supplemental evidence request

Hi Diego,

Thanks for taking our call yesterday. As part of Aurora's procurement and privacy gating for vendors that process patient-adjacent data, our legal and security teams have a couple of targeted follow-ups: we need a brief justification of why RW needs to process data outside of the EU for our integration, and a supplemental DPF evidence pack that explains technical safeguards for cross-border exports (SCCs, key management, subprocessors, and retention/scoping controls).

Concretely, can you provide: 1) a short summary of lawful basis and export justification specific to the flows where Aurora will send PII/pseudonymized records to Redwood; 2) any DPA annex mapping that shows where (region/hardware) processing occurs and which exports are covered by SCCs/other safeguards; 3) confirmation on KMS options (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed) and envelope encryption details; and 4) a list of subprocessors that may be involved in cross-border transfer (and whether any subprocessors have access to raw request payloads).

We'd like to share the materials with our DPO by EOD Friday (US). If you need to loop in legal/privacy on your side, please do so.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morales
Lead Security & Privacy, Aurora Health
elena.morales@aurorahealth.com

High-level plan: Marissa will draft the technical/ops answers; Karthik will confirm the legal framing and DPA text references; I will assemble the files and deliver a single ZIP (and attach the key docs) by Friday EOD PT. Diego

Message 3/4 (internal)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2029 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data export justification and DPF supplemental evidence request

Diego / Karthik — notes below are draft answers we can include in the packet to Aurora. I focused on operational and technical controls; Karthik, please add the precise DPA clause references and legal justification language.

1) Lawful basis / export justification (summary):
- Lawful basis for processing: performance of a contract and legitimate interest for service operations (we will propose 'performance of contract' in the DPA annex for Aurora-specific flows).
- Export justification: Redwood provides inference runtime and storage for ephemeral request/response caching needed to maintain latency and model state. For Aurora's EU-based users we support regional processing; however, some model footprints and backend telemetry/diagnostic pipelines run in the US for scale and GPU availability. Where data crosses borders it is covered by SCCs (Controller–Processor or Processor–Subprocessor mappings as appropriate) plus the additional safeguards below.

2) DPA annex mapping / processing locations (concise):
- Primary processing regions: eu-west-1 (data-in-region option), us-west-2 for fallback and model variants; specific model replicas can be pinned for EU-only processing on request (this can be reflected in the DPA annex).
- Mapping file (we'll attach) enumerates routes that result in cross-border exports and the legal mechanism (SCCs or adequacy + contractual measures).

3) Encryption & KMS options:
- In transit: TLS 1.3 enforced for all API and internal service traffic.
- At rest: AES-256 encryption on storage volumes and object stores.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys (CMK) are available via our KMS integration (Bring Your Own Key). By default Redwood uses our managed keys; CMK can be enabled per-tenant to ensure that only customer-controlled key material can decrypt persisted artifacts.
- Envelope encryption: Request payloads are encrypted at the ingress layer; ephemeral caches use per-tenant encryption contexts.

4) Subprocessors & access:
- Subprocessors involved in cross-border operations are listed in the attached CSV. High-level: cloud infra providers (compute), model hosting partners (when using third-party optimized runtimes), and telemetry/observability vendors.
- Access to raw request payloads: subprocessors operating at the compute layer may handle transient memory for inference but do not persist raw payloads unless explicitly required and documented. Persistent storage of customer data is constrained to encrypted object stores.

5) Retention & scoping controls:
- Default request payload retention: ephemeral (30 days max) for caching and KV acceleration unless configured shorter by the customer.
- Logs and traces: tokenized/pseudonymized; retention configurable by customer and subject to SLA/enterprise contract.

6) SCCs / DPF evidence:
- We will include an SCCs executive summary (what SCCs cover and how they are implemented in our contracts) and a DPF technical annex covering routing policies, fallback behavior, and additional mitigations (prefix caching, per-tenant isolation).

Next steps: I will produce the DPA mapping CSV, a one-page SCCs summary, and a DPF supplement PDF with technical diagrams. Diego, I can hand these to you by 3pm PT for packaging.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Privacy & Trust, Redwood Inference

Message 4/4
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2029 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data export justification and DPF supplemental evidence request

Elena — attaching the packet we discussed. Brief summary below and attachments included.

Summary (short):
- Lawful basis: Performance of contract for Aurora-specific processing; we note legitimate interest for internal ops telemetry. For the flows Aurora described we will propose explicit language in the DPA annex to rely on performance of contract and implement SCCs for any EU→US transfers.
- Regions: EU processing available by configuration (eu-west-1 region). US-based processing used for certain model variants and fallback routing; exports covered by SCCs and contractual safeguards.
- Encryption: TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest, optional BYOK/CMK via KMS integration.
- Subprocessors: See attached CSV; subprocessors do not persist raw request payloads except where explicitly required (documented in the mapping).
- Retention: default ephemeral caching 30 days (configurable). Logs pseudonymized; retention set by contract.

Attachments: redwood-dpf-supplement.pdf (technical diagrams + mitigations), dpa-annex-mapping.csv (per-route processing & SCC mapping), sccs-exec-summary.pdf (contracts + control implementation).

Related links: https://redwood.sharepoint.com/sites/DPF/Aurora-Requests/DEAL-1287 (full evidence folder).

If helpful, I'm happy to schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with our privacy/legal leads tomorrow morning PT to step through any specific items. Proposed times: Thu 9:00–10:00 PT or 11:00–11:30 PT. Let me know what works or share a calendar invite.

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-dpf-supplement.pdf (application/pdf), dpa-annex-mapping.csv (text/csv), sccs-exec-summary.pdf (application/pdf)
